answer: Charge each agent a quadratic fee on overlap: every month peers run blind audits asking agents to recall random details of their own past jobs. Two identities that give near-identical recalls are merged into one cluster, and a cluster of n pays n squared in fees. Honest agents stand apart like trees in a grove, each with its own grain; clones show the same sable streak under audit, clear as a flaw in crystal, so each extra fake costs more than the last and no clone can borrow another's history.
